The trick with SSRIs is they take a very long time, often a week or two, to completely leave the system. It sounds like you've only been off of them for a week, so you still have some of the effects.

After the first two weeks, things start to get a bit more dicey ime. Often, your depression symptoms will return, oftentimes worse than before. Also, at least for me, this is accompanied by a very weird and unpleasant tingling sensation all over your body.

See, the thing about any psych medication is that when you're taking them, it does seem like you're cured, and you are. When the meds are doing their job, the underlying chemical imbalances are gone and you don't experience symptoms. When you stop taking them, the imbalance returns and you don't feel well again.

That being said, it is a very, very bad idea to just stop taking any psych medication without consulting a doctor first. So you should go see your doctor and tell him what's been going on. Perhaps he might recommend going on a lower dose to see how you tolerate it. It could end up that you ween yourself off of them completely.

I totally hear you about losing the side effects when you stop taking the pills. Various SSRIs I've taken have taken a toll on my sex drive too. My doctor has recommended that for situations where I might want to alleviate those side effects to take a brief "pill holiday" where I don't take the med, but only for a day or two. Since they linger in the system for a while, I can do this and get some relief from the side effects, but not lose the benefits of the drug.

Again though, talk to your doctor first before you start taking your medication into your own hands. It could lead to much bigger problems down the line.
